text:
maya: Heads up — customer ACME (acct acme-42) reports a surge of toolcall failures after the v13.2 rollout. Symptoms: schema validation errors from tool invocations, some 500s, and a billing spike from repeated partner calls. They want this triaged ASAP.

amir: Can you paste a sample request_id + payload so eng can repro?

maya: Request_id=rid_20260223_151204. Minimal repro below (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/infer \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{\n    "model":"redwood-model-v13.2",\n    "input":"search for pricing on feature x",\n    "tools":[{"name":"web_search","version":"v2","args":{"q":{"text":"pricing feature x"}}}]\n  }'
```

maya: Log excerpt: 
[2026-02-23T15:12:04Z] request_id=rid_20260223_151204 toolinvoker:web_search v2 ERROR schema_validation failed: expected field "query" (string) but got object "q"; invocation aborted; external partner call still emitted; partner reports duplicate calls.
Billing note: ACME saw partner usage jump ~3x between 15:10-15:20.

ryan: That payload uses the old arg name (q) — v2 expects {"query":"..."}. Was there an adapter in the selector before?

li: Yes. web_search v2 removed backward adapter in selector to reduce overhead, but we had a compatibility shim in runtime. Looks like the v13.2 rollout toggled selector behavior and removed the runtime shim by accident.

amir: Canary size? How widespread?

maya: Canary=8% of traffic; canary error rate=11% vs baseline 0.8%. ACME is in the canary cohort.

eng-runtime: Noted. During the v13.2 canary we pushed a config change that disabled alias fallback for tool selectors (perf optimization). That combined with the missing runtime shim causes direct v2 calls with old args. Root cause: selector config + missing adapter.

ryan: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Reinstate compatibility shim in runtime (hotfix), 2) Re-enable alias fallback on selector (config revert), 3) Rollback v13.2 canary. Which do we do now?

li: I'm going to coordinate a rollback of the canary and re-enable alias fallback as a short-term fix. Will open an incident.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1134. Notified account team and SRE oncall.

infra-bot: Rollback scheduled: job_id=rb-2026-11, targeting canary cohort; start=2026-02-23T15:20:00Z; est duration 2 minutes.

maya: I'll tell the customer we're pausing the canary and will follow up in 10m. +1 from account.

[15:22] infra-bot: Rollback job rb-2026-11 completed. Canary traffic reverted to v13.1.

ryan: Confirm metrics — error rate on canary dropped back to 0.9% within 3 minutes. Partner call volume returned to baseline. Billing anomaly acknowledged by partner and ACME; support will coordinate credits.

li: Action items: (1) eng-runtime to restore compatibility shim or implement argument translation in the selector adapter (owner: eng-runtime); (2) add unit tests for tool arg aliasing; (3) add canary quick-alert when toolcall schema errors spike (>2%); (4) postmortem to document rollout checklist.

eng-runtime: Ack. I'll open PR for shim + tests, and schedule a small canary-config guardrail.

support-bot: Created ticket: TASK-2026-442 (coordination with billing + ACME).

maya: ACME updated: they're relieved for now but want confirmation before we re-roll v13.2. I'll hold their approval.

amir: Recommend a staged rollout with selector fallback enabled, plus automated schema-validation alerts during canary. After that we can reattempt v13.2.

ryan: Agreed. Marking this resolved for now — follow-ups tracked in TASK-2026-442 and INC-2026-1134. :white_check_mark:

li: Thanks everyone. We'll keep updates in the incident thread. :pray:
